away.name: Yaroslav Askarov
away.news: Despite team struggles, Askarov had strung together several strong outings before his worst performance of the season in San Jose's most recent game, allowing seven goals on 26 shots (.731 SV%) in a 7-2 loss to the Los Angeles Kings. Still, the 24-year-old Russian goalie has a 2.69 GAA and .914 SV% in his last six games (2-4-0). The Sharks enter Friday's action as significant +234 road underdogs against the 11-3-3 Central Division-leading Minnesota Wild.

home.name: Jesper Wallstedt
home.news: Wallstedt has been busy with Filip Gustavsson (hip) sidelined and will return to the crease for the 16th time in Minnesota's first 18 games. The 23-year-old Swedish goalie has been outstanding to start the 2026-27 season, giving Head Coach John Hynes no reason to deviate, posting a stellar 2.06 GAA and .920 SV% in 15 games (10-2-3). In his last six games (4-1-1), Gustavsson has allowed two or fewer goals five times. Minnesota enters Friday's outing as a sizeable -273 home favourite against a struggling San Jose Sharks team that has scored only seven goals combined in their past five games (1-4-0).

away.name: Lukas Dostal
away.news: Dostal will start in Calgary on Friday.

home.name: Dustin Wolf
home.news: The Flames were leaning on Devin Cooley before his lower-body injury, but now, upon his return, they will roll with Wolf, who was solid in Cooley's absence. The 25-year-old Wolf saved 27 of 29 shots (.931 SV%) in his most recent outing, a 2-1 overtime loss to the Seattle Kraken. In his last three games (2-0-1), he has a stellar 1.69 GAA and .936 SV%. The Flames enter Friday's game as -140 home favourites against an Anaheim Ducks team that has been thriving offensively, scoring five or more goals in six straight games (4-1-1).
